quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 16 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: When riding through a curve, you should:

options.text: Stay in the same part of the lane the whole time.
Stay in the left part of the lane the whole time.
Stay in the right part of the lane the whole time.
Know that the best path may not follow the road's curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know that the best path may not follow the road's curve.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change all the time. Be ready to move to a different lane position when needed. The best path through a curve may not match the curve of the road.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Signs that show road rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When a group of motorcyclists rides through a curve, they should:
questions.explanation: While staggered formation is usually best, a group should switch to single-file when riding through curves, turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane give a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane has three paths for motorcyclists: the left part, the center part, and the right part of the lane.

questions.question: Where should a load be placed on a motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them tightly or put them in saddlebags. Placing loads high on a sissy bar or back of the seat is unsafe because it raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and makes it harder to balance. Always spread loads evenly on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist stop other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride in the left part of the lane.
Ride in the center part of the lane.
Give dirty looks if another driver moves into the lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center part of the lane.
questions.explanation: When another driver might try to squeeze into your lane next to you, ride in the center part of the lane. This discourages them from sharing your space.

questions.question: Where should a child passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: A child does not need to reach the footrests.
The child should hold onto the motorcycle frame.

questions.explanation: A child should always sit right behind the operator. If a child sits in front, they may not balance well and could get in the way of the operator's controls.

questions.question: The front brake provides what percentage of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and provides at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should you always avoid?

options.text: The left part of the lane
The center part of the lane
The right part of the lane
No part should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No part should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best, and no lane position should always be avoided. Choose a lane position that fits the riding conditions.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see others and be seen.

questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and surface hazards. Your lane position should discourage drivers from sharing your lane and always give you an escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Start slowing down earlier than usual.
Talk to the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk to the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. This makes it slower to respond. When carrying a passenger, ride slower than normal, slow down sooner, and stay farther behind other vehicles. Always warn your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When turning left, what should you do?

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.explanation: A motorcycle leans to turn. To make it lean in the direction you want to go, press the handgrip on that side.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may tempt the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see at night. What should a rider do?

options.text: Stay directly in front of another vehicle to use their headlights.

questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down, increase your following distance, and use headlights of other vehicles to see ahead. Use your high beam unless you are following or meeting another vehicle. Be ready to change your lane position.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you must brake and swerve, do them separately. Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: When stopping, what is best to do?

options.text: Grab the front brake lever hard.
Keep your knees on the gas tank and look ahead.
Apply more and more pressure to the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees on the gas tank and look ahead.
questions.explanation: For the best straight-line stop, apply both brakes smoothly and firmly. As weight moves forward, the front wheel has more grip, so increase front brake pressure while decreasing rear brake pressure. Keep your knees on the gas tank and your eyes up to stay in a straight line.
